newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 16.

text.p: Chainsaw used in attack on barman: A chainsaw and an axe were used on Sunday when a man was attacked outside what locals said was an illegal bar in Wainuiomata. Page 1.

Health fight looms for MPs: A report from the steering group set up to advise on implementation of Coalition health policy is shaping up as the next battleground for Health Minister Bill English and his NZ First associate, Neil Kirton. Page 2.

Call for information about Treaty process: The National Party had asked government to improve its communication of its Treaty of Waitangi settlement process to non-Maoris, party president Geoff Thompson said on Sunday. Page 2.

Fiji forests provide opportunity: Fiji's large hardwood plantations will soon be ready for harvest, and International Trade Minister Lockwood Smith says New Zealand could become involved in joint ventures to use the wood. Page 13.
Brash defends low inflation: Reserve Bank governor Don Brash said he had no doubt that interest rates would continue a downward trend as New Zealand built up a record for low inflation. Page 13.

DFS plans new stores: Duty and tax-free retailer DFS New Zealand said it would almost double retail space through the construction of new stores and Auckland and Christchurch international airports and the opening of a new central city Auckland store. Page 15.
Paydirt proves elusive for DML: DML Resources has not won a new mining contract since it was taken over 15 months ago as part of the leveraged buyout of its parent Skellerup Group.

Enthusiastic reception for tower transmission power: Auckland's newest landmark, the Sky Tower, is set to become one of the country's most important communications links as competing telecommunications companies, television, FM radio, courier and taxi firms take advantage of its height.

China becomes central to Nat Mutual's plans: National Mutual expects China to be a central part of its Asian growth strategy, despite its French parent Axa-UAP getting the nod for the group's first licence to operate in China.

Fernz sizes up deal with Rhone: Fernz Corporation is likely to form a joint venture with France's Rhone Poulene to control the global market for chemicals that combat weed crops, Fernz chief executive Kerry Hoggard has signalled.
Paper chase for companies may soon be over: The Companies Office may move to a fully electronic company register, as has been done in Canada.
Due to technical difficulties we have been unable to bring The Press digest this morning.
